newsitem.title: UK: UK disappointed by European Court Saunders ruling.
newsitem.headline: UK disappointed by European Court Saunders ruling.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said it was disappointed by a European Court of Human Rights ruling that Britain had denied a fair trial to Ernest Saunders, former chairman of Guinness Plc, who was convicted of fraud in 1990.
"The government is disappointed that the court has found there was a violation of the convention in the trial of Ernest Saunders," said a DTI spokeswoman.
Saunders argued that he was unfairly convicted because evidence obtained by Department of Trade and Industry investigators under compulsion was used in court.

"Mr Saunders was convicted by jury after it had heard all the evidence. The court of appeal has carefully reviewed his case on two occasions and on both occasions the convictions were found to be safe and satisfactory," said the DTI spokeswoman.
